title: Common conceptual misconception
label: Demo data — synthetic
question: Does the existence of a limit at x = c imply the function must be continuous at x = c?
student_answer: Yes, if the limit exists at x = c, then the function is automatically continuous at that point because the graph must connect smoothly.

chunks.text: A function is continuous at c if and only if lim_{x->c} f(x) exists, f(c) is defined, and lim_{x->c} f(x) = f(c). A removable discontinuity has a valid limit but fails continuity.
